title: Dictionaries: a contact sheet
hook: Look things up by name, like a contact sheet: name in, phone number out.

warmup.explain: sum adds the numbers in the list: 2 + 3 + 5 = 10.

warmup.q: `for item in names:` the name `item` holds...
options: One item at a time, in turn
warmup.explain: Each time around the loop, item is the next item in the list.
int turns the text 12 into the number 12. Then plus 1 is 13.

why.heading: Lists find by position
why.text: With a list you ask for spot 0, spot 1, spot 2. But on set you never say 'give me spot 4'. You say 'give me Thandi's number'. You want to look things up by **name**, not by position.

why.heading: A contact sheet in code
why.text:
A **dictionary** pairs a name with a thing. The name is the **key**. The thing is the **value**.

`phones = {"Sam": "0821", "Thandi": "0832"}`

Curly brackets. Key, a colon, value. Commas between pairs.

why.heading: Look up, add, change
why.text:
Look up with the key in square brackets: `phones["Sam"]` gives `0821`.

Add or change with the same shape on the left of an equals sign:

`phones["Lebo"] = "0843"`

If Lebo is new, he is added. If the key exists, its value is replaced.

why.heading: KeyError and .get
why.text:
Ask for a key that is not there and Python says **KeyError**. It means: no such name on the sheet. The safe way is `.get`:

`phones.get("Zed", "unknown")`

It gives back your fallback (`unknown`) instead of an error.

why.heading: Loop through the pairs
why.text:
To go through the whole sheet, use `.items()`:

`for name, num in phones.items():`

Each turn you get one key and its value together, like `enumerate` gave you a number and an item.

watch.intro: Tap Run. Crew day rates by job, looked up, changed and looped.
watch.code:
rates = {"gaffer": 1800, "grip": 1200, "sound": 1500}
print(rates["gaffer"])
rates["grip"] = 1300
rates["editor"] = 1400
print(rates.get("drone pilot", "not listed"))
for job, pay in rates.items():
    print(f"{job}: R{pay}")
explain: `rates["gaffer"]` looks up the key and gives its value, 1800.
`rates["grip"] = 1300` changes an existing key. `rates["editor"] = 1400` adds a new one.
`.get` with a fallback is safe when the key might be missing.
`.items()` gives each key and value in turn, in the order they were added.
watch.break_it: Break it on purpose: add the line `print(rates["drone pilot"])` at the bottom and tap Run. The error ends with `KeyError: 'drone pilot'`. That key is not on the sheet. Change it to `.get` and it stops being an error.

tasks.title: Find a contact, then list all
tasks.task:
Ask `Who? `. Print that person's number, or `No such contact` if they are not on the sheet. Then print everyone as `Name: number`, one per line. Example with `Thandi`:

`Who? Thandi`
`0832`
`Sam: 0821`
`Thandi: 0832`
`Lebo: 0843`
hints: Use phones.get(name, "No such contact") so a missing name does not crash.
For the full list use: for n, num in phones.items():
Inside the loop: print(f"{n}: {num}"). Do the .get line before the loop.

recap: A dictionary pairs keys with values: `{"Sam": "0821"}`.
`d[key]` looks up. `d[key] = value` adds or changes.
`d.get(key, fallback)` is safe when the key may be missing. A missing key with `[ ]` gives KeyError.
`for k, v in d.items():` loops through every pair.
